Commentary.Commentary: Here we go! The players and the umpires walk out to the middle to start the run chase! it is the pair of Kusal Mendis and Pathum Nissanka to open the batting for Sri Lanka who have the task to chase 173 runs in 20 overs. Matt Henry has the new ball in hand and is ready at the bowler's mark to start the innings. Let's Play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The stage is now set for an intriguing chase. Can Sri Lanka's batters rise to the occasion and chase down 173, or will New Zealand's bowlers step up to secure a victory for their side? The second inning promises to be an exciting contest. Stay tuned as we return back with the run chase!

Daryl Mitchell is in for a chat. He says that the new ball was doing a little bit and after losing a few wickets early, it was about building a partnership. Mentions that Michael Bracewell did what he does best. Feels that on a bigger ground like this one, it is important to use the pockets and collect twos to put the bowlers under pressure. Reckons that Powerplay will be crucial and it will be important for the pacers to hit the deck hard and extract extra bounce.

Bracewell led the recovery with a superb knock of 59 runs off just 33 deliveries, showcasing a mix of calculated aggression and smart shot selection. Mitchell provided equally vital support, hammering 62 off 42 balls. Their partnership was marked by exceptional running between the wickets and powerful hitting, helping New Zealand recover from early setbacks and reach a strong total under challenging circumstances. Mitchell was eventually dismissed in the final over, but his efforts, along with Bracewell's, ensured New Zealand had a defendable target on the board.

Sri Lanka began strongly with the ball, as Binura Fernando delivered an impressive opening spell, claiming two wickets in his first three overs and pushing New Zealand onto the back foot. Wanindu Hasaranga further tightened the screws after the Powerplay, striking twice in quick succession to leave New Zealand struggling. Sri Lanka maintained control of the game for the first 10 overs, but the tide turned with the arrival of Bracewell at the crease.

A good last over for Sri Lanka but this is an excellent recovery from New Zealand, posting a competitive total of 172 runs for the loss of eight wickets in 20 overs, thanks to a game-changing partnership between Daryl Mitchell and Michael Bracewell. After a shaky start that saw New Zealand reeling at 65/5 by the halfway mark, the duo combined for a stellar 105-run stand that revived their innings and shifted the momentum.

OUT! RUN OUT! A run out to end the New Zealand innings! A fantastic over from Maheesh Theekshana. Stays around the wicket for the right-hander and angles it across, on a nagging length, Zakary Foulkes drags it across in front of deep mid-wicket and decides to come back for the second run. Kamindu Mendis swoops in off the ropes and picks the ball up with his left hand. Fires in a throw on the bounce to the keeper. The throw is a bit wide but Kusal Mendis does well to collect the throw and take the bails off. It is referred upstairs and the replays show that Foulkes is short of his crease despite the dive. Just 3 runs off the 20th over. New Zealand finish with 172 on the board.

Mitchell holds the key here for the Kiwis to get to a competitive total while the tourists will look to continue to chip away at the wickets. Mitchell Hay joins Daryl Mitchell out in the centre.

A big, big shout for LBW but the umpire shakes his head! Wanindu Hasaranga is convinced and Charith Asalanka takes the review. Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the action to start. Charith Asalanka and his men stride out to the centre. Tim Robinson and Rachin Ravindra will open the innings for New Zealand. Nuwan Thushara will kickstart proceedings with the new ball for Sri Lanka. A slip in place. Let's play...

We are moments away from the first ball, but before that, Mitchell Santner and Charith Asalanka lead their respective sides out along with their mascots for the national anthems. It will be Sri Lanka's national anthem first, followed by the national anthem of New Zealand.

The skipper of New Zealand, Mitchell Santner says that the wicket usually plays well here but there is a bit of a green tinge on this surface. Informs that Bevon Jacobs and Nathan Smith miss out. Mentions that they enjoy playing at home as a unit and are looking forward to playing in front of a sell-out crowd. Feels that they have a good schedule leading up to the Champions Trophy.

The captain of Sri Lanka, Charith Asalanka says that the wicket looks decent to bat and won't change much. Adds that they will look to chase. He further adds that the conditions here are very different and they will look to adapt as soon as possible. Finally, he talks about keeping things simple and taking 1 game at a time. He shares that the team is in good form and they will look to dominate straight away
